newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close down on domestic ban.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close down on domestic ban.

text.p: Shanghai B shares closed down slightly on Monday after the authorities banned domestic investors from buying new B shares, but brokers said the news had largely been digested thanks to recent rumours.
Brokers said that the news hurt market sentiment further because most trading is now done by domestic investors.
The index shed 0.287 points or 0.58 percent to 49.059 points, on volume of 9.0 million shares worth $3.6 million. Of 41 B shares, 32 traded, with 16 down, eight flat and eight up.
The Shanghai Stock Exchange published a notice last Friday banning domestic investors from buying new B shares but allowing them to sell.

"The ban means that the market will experience a bearish trend with overseas funds withdrawing their capital from the market," one broker said. "But some domestic insitutions were supporting the market as they have large positions."
"Further drastic falls are unlikely in the short term as the news has been digested in previous weeks," a second broker said.
"Domestic investors will not sell their shares as the index is already too low," he added.
Shanghai Steel Tube was the biggest loser on its unpromising results, falling $0.006 or 4.68 percent to $0.122 on volume of 83,000 shares.
Market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui made up most of its morning losses thanks to one domestic institution's support, falling $0.002 or 0.22 percent to $0.894 on volume of 900,400 shares.
Tientsin Marine traded the most on institutional cross-trading, falling $0.004 or 1.28 percent to $0.308 on volume of 3.2 million shares.
Shanghai A shares soared on rumours that the exchange would cut trading fees, which attracted fresh capital inflows from the Shenzhen market, brokers said.

The A index rose 50.103 points or 5.94 percent to 893.555 points, on volume of 837.2 million shares worth 8.2 billion yuan. The blue-chip SSE 30 index jumped 179.355 points or 8.15 percent to 2380.006 points.
Shenma Industry was the star on institutional speculative buying, surging 1.45 yuan or 19.46 percent to 8.90 yuan, on volume of 18.2 million shares.
